residual: Per-target rows. /rubric on the Robert task asked for one row per issue where each issue's comment or state turned on its own records. Here the 68 creates, 14 moves and 28 lines are sampled. The writes are template-identical apart from the item's own words and its decided state, and every item whose state turns on a record other than its own tick, every hold and both Covered ties has a direct row (rubric_sampling: repetitive items of comparable importance). If /rubric asks for a row per item, copy its Fix List exactly; such rows mostly pass and would raise the average and lower the SD.

Weights of the ordinary samples at 1 (P8–P12 ticks, P32–P36 moves, P43, P55–P57 shares). /rubric accepted the same weight for ordinary moves and shares on the Robert task, but it may read a rule applied to one target as 3 (Frederick round 1). Eleven rows one level off would be 18 % and fail Weights, so check its weight table first.
P6 at 5 and P46 at 3. Both count one audit's output; P46 compares the population with the notes' scope tests (Robert's item-row count was accepted at 3), while P6 needs every item's decision.

P2–P5 and P42 grade one property on every member of a population ('every new … issue', 'all 28 UI children'). These are template volume controls, not exact-set rows. If the builder's imported atomicity lint flags them, mark the flag invalid with rubric_sampling's volume-control rule rather than splitting.

The sheet's Outcome and Ticket groups (G7, G8) hold edge samples only. rubric_sampling treats a weak sample choice as a note, not a finding; every ordinary Fixed item is graded on its Linear state (P8–P12).
